race.name: Rule of Three
race.tagline: Bentonville's three-surface problem: tarmac speed, sharp Ozark gravel, and climby singletrack on one bike.

climate.description: Mid-May in Northwest Arkansas can move between warm, humid conditions and thunderstorms. The inaugural 2021 event followed a week of rain and sent roughly 650 riders onto muddy terrain. The 2027 forecast cannot be known this far out.
challenges: Mud and wet roots on singletrack
Rapidly changing traction across three surfaces

terrain.surface: The defining format combines pavement, gravel, and singletrack. The organizer describes sharp rock, technical B-roads, loose gravel descents, steep and climby trails, and frequent surface changes. It creates a new course every year and withholds the route until closer to the event, so 2026 mile-by-mile details must not be projected onto 2027.
features: One-bike compromise across tarmac, gravel, and singletrack
Sharp Ozark rock and puncture risk
Climby, flowy trail sectors ridden under fatigue
Unmarked gravel and pavement sections requiring GPS navigation

biased_opinion.verdict: One Bike, Three Different Bad Ideas
biased_opinion.summary: Rule of Three is a Bentonville mixed-surface event. Its identity is the equipment and pacing compromise created by pavement, sharp gravel, and meaningful singletrack in the same day. The organizer changes the route annually, keeps the community deliberately playful, and still gives the flagship field a technically serious problem.
strengths: Technical demand beyond a conventional gravel race
weaknesses: The annual late route reveal complicates specific preparation
No single bike or tire choice is ideal everywhere
Navigation matters because most gravel and pavement is not marked
Spring rain can transform both B-roads and singletrack
The flagship takes much longer than an ordinary road-heavy 115-miler
biased_opinion.bottom_line: Race it if choosing and handling one bike across three incompatible surfaces sounds interesting. Wait for the 2027 route before making course-specific claims or finalizing a race-week plan.

logistics.alternate_airports: Tulsa International Airport (TUL), roughly two hours by car
logistics.lodging_note: Bentonville and nearby Rogers have hotels and rentals; the organizer has historically offered limited on-site camping.
logistics.parking: Historically at the Price Coffee Road venue; final 2027 instructions pending
logistics.travel_summary: Bentonville is accessible through XNA and has extensive cycling infrastructure. A rental car is useful for the event venue and wider Northwest Arkansas trail network.
logistics.food_options: Bentonville and Rogers have extensive pre- and post-race options; organizer aid and finish details are pending
logistics.camping: Historically available at the event venue with limited facilities; verify the 2027 rider guide

course_description.character: A long, irregular sequence of tarmac, gravel, technical B-roads, and climby singletrack. Speed on one surface creates fatigue and handling consequences on the next. The 2027 route is not yet published.

suffering_zones.name: Every Surface Change
suffering_zones.description: Position, tire pressure, gearing, and handling priorities change repeatedly; settling into one rhythm is the wrong expectation.
suffering_zones.survival_strategy: Practice transitions between fast pavement, loose gravel, and singletrack on the same bike.

suffering_zones.name: Late Singletrack
suffering_zones.description: The organizer deliberately places meaningful trail riding after accumulated fatigue.
suffering_zones.survival_strategy: Train technical focus and low-cadence climbing after long mixed-surface rides.

suffering_zones.name: Navigation and Equipment Attrition
suffering_zones.description: Most gravel and pavement is not marked, while sharp rock and technical sectors punish fragile tires and poor line choice.
suffering_zones.survival_strategy: Use durable tubeless tires, carry complete repair tools, and rehearse GPS navigation.

course_description.signature_challenge: Choosing one setup—and preserving enough concentration—to be fast on pavement, durable on sharp gravel, and capable on steep singletrack.

history.origin_story: The concept grew from riding Allied ABLE prototypes across Bentonville pavement, gravel, and singletrack. The first event sold out and drew roughly 650-700 riders despite a wet race week.
notable_moments: 2021: inaugural edition after a rain-soaked week, with roughly 650-700 riders
2026: flagship expanded to 115 miles with 60- and 35-mile options
history.reputation: A hard but intentionally playful Bentonville fixture built around mixed surfaces, equipment choice, and community rather than a conventional gravel-racing template.

logistics.explanation: XNA is close and Bentonville is bike-friendly, but the venue is not a major hub and final 2027 packet, parking, camping, and start instructions are pending.

length.explanation: The established flagship is 115 miles, but the mixed surfaces make elapsed time substantially longer than an ordinary 115-mile gravel route.

technicality.explanation: The organizer describes technical B-roads, loose gravel descents, steep singletrack, sharp rock, and roughly 25 miles of trail in the established flagship format.

elevation.explanation: The organizer consistently describes relentless, steep, and climby terrain, but has not published 2027 total ascent; the score reflects character without inventing a number.

climate.explanation: Northwest Arkansas spring weather can bring humidity, thunderstorms, mud, and wet roots; the first edition followed a week of rain.

altitude.explanation: Bentonville is a low-altitude event, so elevation above sea level is not a meaningful limiter.

adventure.explanation: A single day that deliberately links tarmac, remote gravel and B-roads, and real singletrack creates an unusually varied challenge.

prestige.explanation: It is a well-known sold-out regional fixture with national reach, but not a championship or top global professional target.

race_quality.explanation: The established event pairs serious route design with aid stations, navigation instructions, team formats, and explicit safety systems.

experience.explanation: The three-surface identity, finish-line party, unusual awards, and Bentonville setting are distinct rather than interchangeable with a standard gravel fondo.

community.explanation: The organizer explicitly centers kindness, team participation, volunteers, gifts for strangers, aid-station culture, and a long finish-line gathering.

field_depth.explanation: The event sold out its first edition and attracts riders nationally, but official current field size and elite depth are not published.

value.explanation: The organizer designs sponsor participation around rider value and a full event-week experience, though the 2027 entry fee is not yet published.

expenses.explanation: Domestic access through XNA is reasonable, but travel, lodging, and a durable mixed-surface bike setup still make this more than a local low-cost day.

final_verdict.one_liner: A technically serious three-surface race hiding inside Bentonville's friendliest strange bike party.
final_verdict.should_you_race: Yes if mixed-surface handling, equipment compromise, and a community-first event appeal to you. The date is confirmed, but wait for the annual route release before treating any prior year's mileage, climbing, sector order, or schedule as final.
final_verdict.alternatives: Core4 uses a similarly deliberate multi-surface concept, while Big Sugar offers a larger Bentonville gravel race without making singletrack one-third of the identity.
